units.summary: New test. It evicts a non-stale series through CompactSelectedSeries, forces a WAL checkpoint with mint between the head's min and max time, and asserts that the evicted series's record stays in the checkpoint. It is test-only and cannot affect production.
units.headline: Test checks checkpoint keeps evicted selected-series record
units.reason: New test only; no production code changes.

units.summary: gcStaleSeries is renamed to gcSeries and now takes a shouldEvict predicate, so it serves both stale and selected-series eviction. numStaleSeries is now reduced only by the number of deleted series that were actually stale, not by every deleted series. This matches how the regular GC path already updates the counter.
units.headline: Head GC takes eviction predicate; stale counter decrements accurately
units.reason: Changes how series are evicted and how head metrics are accounted for.
focus: numStaleSeries stays correct when both stale and non-stale series are evicted in one call
the WAL expiry and tombstone handling further down still applies to every deleted ref

units.summary: The hard-coded stale-NaN check is replaced by the caller's shouldEvict predicate, which runs after the maxTime > maxt safety check. The function also counts deleted series that were stale, using isStaleSeries while the series lock is held. Both callers (stale and selected truncation) pass predicates that also check for OOO data and the appendID watermark.
units.headline: Stripe GC uses caller predicate instead of hard-coded stale check
units.reason: Generalizes which series can be deleted from the head, a core data-retention decision.
focus: shouldEvict runs with series.Lock held, which hasAppendIDAbove requires
the stale-head path keeps its stale check through the truncateStaleSeries predicate
